en.title: Earliest Time the Number of Malicious-Character Substrings Reaches a Threshold
en.description:
The initial lowercase password has length n. At second t, position attackOrder[t] (1-based) is changed to *, and attackOrder is a permutation of 1..n. A damaged substring is a non-empty contiguous substring containing at least one *, counted separately by start and end positions. Find the second at which their number first reaches or exceeds m. When m=0, output 1, as specially required by the source. The source's main text mistakenly wrote the threshold as n; it is corrected according to the parameter m and both examples.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n m, the second line the password, and the third line n values attackOrder. 1≤n≤800000, 0≤m≤n(n+1)/2, the password is lowercase, and attackOrder is a permutation of 1..n.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 2, 4 and 1. In the first example there are 8 damaged substrings at second 1 and 11 at second 2, which is the first time the count reaches 10.
hints: Undo the attacks in reverse order, turning every position from bad back to good. Maintain the length of each good contiguous segment at its two ends; when a position is activated, read the left and right lengths L and R, and the newly created all-good substrings number exactly (L+1)(R+1). When the damaged count drops from ≥m to <m, the time before that undo is the answer.
